title: Intake Processing Backlog for New Finds
dataSources: Collection items (`collection:item`), intake scans (`collection:scan`), market prices (`collection:price`), item photos (`collection:photo`), authentication records (`collection:auth`), loans (`collection:loan`), and condition audits (`collection:condition`).
app: Collection telemetry from personal catalogues, NFC scans, pricing feeds, authentication records, loan logs, shelf measurements, and item-condition audits streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=collection:scan status="unprocessed"
| stats count as pending_items by collection_type source
| sort - pending_items
description: Counts newly acquired items that have been scanned but not yet fully catalogued.
value: Collectors often buy faster than they process, and a visible backlog helps keep the collection database trustworthy.
implementation: Log a quick intake scan when an item arrives and mark it processed only after metadata, condition, and location are filled in.
visualization: Bar chart of pending intake items by collection type and source.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how many newly found items are still waiting to be properly added to your collection records.
